title: PRD: Hosted Endpoint Behavior Bands, Scoped Acceptance & Cutover Checklist
creator: Asha Patel
description: High-level PRD defining behavior bands (Quality / Cost / Latency tiers) for hosted inference endpoints (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank). Documents explicit acceptance criteria, scoped cutover checklist, rollback triggers, and operational runbooks required for go-live. This ticket synthesizes PM decisions, engineering constraints, design notes, and QA requirements into a single acceptance artifact for the launch tranche.
background: Customers ask for consistent, predictable behavior across generation and retrieval endpoints while controlling cost. Prior PRDs focused on surface and contracts; this doc codifies graded guarantees (behavior bands) and the acceptance flow that gates launch. Recent incidents showed silent regressions when models or kernel sets changed—we need formalized acceptance and rollback guardrails.
scope: Define three behavior bands: Premium (low-latency/high-quality), Balanced (cost-optimized), Economical (min-cost with graceful degradation)
Behavior band mapping per endpoint: chat, completions, embeddings, rerank
Acceptance test matrix (functional + perf + cost) for each band
Cutover checklist for staged rollout with canaries and traffic slicing
Operational playbooks for detected regressions and automatic fallbacks
out_of_scope: New model onboarding pipeline (handled in separate onboarding PRD)
Deep UX redesigns for Console (only telemetry surfaces required)
requirements: API contract compatibility: no breaking changes to request/response shapes for GA clients
Per-route quality profile: example prompts + expected top-line metrics (BLEU/ROUGE/Embedding cosine) per band
Latency SLOs per band (P50/P95) and cost-per-1k-tokens targets
Canary traffic gating with automated abort on regression thresholds
Deterministic eval harness that can be applied to new runtime builds and model variants
Telemetries: per-route token breakdown, model variant, kernel set, and region
acceptance_criteria: Functional parity: chat/completions/responders return expected structured fields for 100% of regression test cases
Quality thresholds: Premium band mean eval score >= 0.92 (primary eval), Balanced >= 0.86, Economical >= 0.75 on the seeded prompt set
Performance SLOs: Premium P95 < 220ms for typical short requests (<=128 tokens), Balanced P95 < 380ms, Economical P95 < 700ms
Cost targets: Measured token cost within +/-10% of predicted cost profile for each band under synthetic workload
End-to-end canary pass: 3 consecutive canary cycles (1h each) with no alert-level regressions and no customer-facing errors
Rollback criteria defined and tested: automatic rollback triggers on SLI breaches (latency/quality/error-rate) and manual abort paths verified
Security: SSO/SAML sign-in flow and KMS-backed key provisioning validated in private deployment sims
Observability: dashboards show per-band KPIs and traces for sampled requests during canary
launch_checklist: Finalize band-to-model mapping and annotate in model catalog (owner: Applied ML)
Run seeded deterministic eval across the full prompt suite for candidate runtime (owner: QA)
Execute load-profiled canary with traffic slices (10% of slice A, 1% overall) and run 3 cycles
Confirm cost telemetry math on sample billing dashboard and validate cost alarms (owner: Finance)
Designate rollback owner and confirm pet tests for rollback validation
Complete security sign-off and record artifacts (SAML integration tests + KMS logs)
Update API docs and client SDK changelog to include band parameter and example mappings (owner: Dev Rel)
Schedule staged open beta and invite top 10 early customers for verification
Post-launch monitoring plan and 48hr on-call SME rota established
risks: Quality regressions due to unseen prompt distribution—mitigation: expand eval prompt diversity and run A/B on production traffic
Cost spike if batching heuristics differ between canary and production—mitigation: synthetic finance checks and pre-prod cost simulation
False positives in automated guards (trigger rollback erroneously)—mitigation: dual-threshold aborts (soft alert then hard abort) and human-in-loop validation
Model variant mismatches across regions—mitigation: per-region canaries and model registry pinning
dependencies: DES-5612 (API surface microcopy for band parameter)
